result.title: Mesh-Free Keypoint Learning for Category-Level 6D Object Pose Estimation
result.summary: Category-level 6D pose estimation relates partial RGB-D observations of unseen instances to a canonical frame shared across a category. Object-aware reconstruction helps adaptive keypoints retain the geometry of the visible surface. Common reconstruction targets select observed points by their distance to a registered instance surface. We present MORSEPose, which derives this support directly from standard pose and metric-size annotations. We map observed 3D points to normalized object coordinates and retain those inside a tolerancedilated pose-and-size envelope. This construction is consistent across camera frames and metric scales. When the annotated extent bounds the object surface, the envelope conservatively contains the support of a conventional surface-distance selector. We integrate this target with multi-level RGB-D features, adaptive keypoints, and learnable category context. Experiments on REAL275 and HouseCat6D show that the envelope closely matches surface-based supervision at both point and task levels, remains stable under boundary perturbations and viewpoint changes, and supports competitive category-level pose accuracy across benchmarks.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 MORSEPose：由位姿与尺寸标注构造带容差的膨胀包络来筛选观测点作为重建支撑，结合多级 RGB-D 特征、自适应关键点和可学习类别上下文做类别级 6D 位姿估计，并在 REAL275、HouseCat6D 上验证。
